title: E-Invoice Portal: Registration, Login & IRP Options Explained
summary: E-invoice portal registration: step-by-step process, common mistakes and the faster way to do it in billing software. Simple guide for MSMEs.
body_markdown:
The **einvoice portal** is where eligible GST-registered businesses report invoice details to obtain an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and a digitally signed QR code. If your business is new to e-invoicing, understanding how to register, log in, and choose an authorised Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) is the first step.


The process can be confusing for first-time users. You may already have a GST login but not an e-invoice account, or your GSTIN may not appear enabled even though your business has crossed the applicable turnover threshold.


This guide explains the **e invoice registration** process, the difference between GST and e-invoice portals, the available IRP options, common login problems, and how billing software like GimBooks can simplify ongoing e-invoice generation.


## **What Is the E-Invoice Portal and Who Needs to Register?**


The **e invoice gst portal** is part of India's GST e-invoicing system. It allows eligible taxpayers to register specified invoice details electronically and receive an IRN and signed QR code from an authorised IRP.


An important distinction is that e-invoicing does not mean creating an invoice directly on the government website. Businesses generally prepare invoices using their existing billing or accounting systems and then report the required data to an IRP for authentication.


### **Who Must Use the E-Invoice System?**


As of November 2026, the e-invoicing requirement generally applies to notified GST-registered taxpayers whose aggregate annual turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017–18 onward, subject to the applicable exemptions and transaction rules.


For example:


- A trading business that crossed ₹5 crore turnover in FY 2023–24 may be covered even if its current turnover is lower.
- A business operating from multiple states must consider turnover across GST registrations under the same PAN.
- A taxpayer belonging to an exempt category may not be required to issue e-invoices despite meeting the turnover threshold.


The requirement generally covers specified B2B invoices, credit notes, debit notes, exports, SEZ supplies, and deemed exports.


If you're unsure whether your business qualifies, read GimBooks' detailed[₹5 crore e-invoice turnover rule guide](https://www.gimbooks.com/blog/5-crore-e-invoice-turnover-rule-2026/) before starting registration.

## **Before You Start: Details Needed for E-Invoice Registration**


Before starting **GST e invoice registration** , confirm that your registration details are updated and that you can access the mobile number and email address associated with your GST account.

You do not ordinarily need to upload documents such as PAN cards, Aadhaar cards, or incorporation certificates just to create a basic IRP account. Most taxpayer details are retrieved through the GSTIN.


However, different IRPs may have additional onboarding requirements for specific integrations or services.


### **Check Whether Your GSTIN Is Enabled**


Before registering, visit the[official GST e-Invoice information portal](https://einvoice.gst.gov.in/) and use its taxpayer enablement facility.


Enter your GSTIN and review the displayed status.


If your GSTIN is enabled, you can proceed with the applicable IRP registration process.


If your GSTIN is not enabled but your business is legally covered, use the available self-enablement facility or follow official portal support instructions.


**Remember:** A GSTIN appearing as enabled does not automatically prove that e-invoicing is legally mandatory for that business. You must independently check turnover, exemptions, and transaction applicability.


## **How to Register on the E-Invoice Portal: Step-by-Step**


If you're searching for **how to register on e invoice portal** , the process generally involves GSTIN verification, OTP authentication, and creating user credentials.


The following walkthrough focuses on the NIC Invoice Registration Portal used by many Indian businesses.


### **Step 1: Visit the Official Invoice Registration Portal**


Open the[official NIC e-Invoice Portal](https://einvoice1.gst.gov.in/) in your browser.


On the homepage, locate the Registration option or the new-user registration link available through the login interface.


### **Step 2: Select the E-Invoice Registration Option**


Choose the taxpayer registration option applicable to your account.


Depending on the interface, this may appear as an e-invoice registration menu or a new-user registration link.


If you already use the NIC e-way bill system, check whether your existing credentials work before creating another account.


### **Step 3: Enter Your GSTIN and Captcha**


The **einvoice registration** form generally asks you to enter:


- Your 15-digit GSTIN
- The displayed captcha or verification code


Submit the information to retrieve the registered taxpayer details.


If the system indicates that your GSTIN is not enabled, verify your e-invoicing applicability and complete the enablement process before attempting registration again.


### **Step 4: Verify Your Business Details**


Once the GSTIN is accepted, the system retrieves relevant information from GST records.


Review the legal name, trade name, registered contact information, and other available details.


If the information is outdated, check whether the portal offers a facility to refresh taxpayer details from the GST Common Portal.


For corrections to the underlying registration information, use the applicable GST amendment process.


### **Step 5: Complete OTP Verification**


Request an OTP using the verification option provided.


The portal may authenticate the registered mobile number and email address as part of its onboarding process.


Enter the requested OTP and complete verification.


If you do not receive the OTP, check whether your registered contact information is current. Avoid repeatedly requesting new OTPs without checking the previous request's status.


### **Step 6: Create Your Username and Password**


After successful verification, create the login credentials permitted by the portal.


Choose a username that satisfies the displayed requirements and create a strong password.


Save the registration details securely.


For businesses with multiple accountants or billing operators, avoid sharing the main account password unnecessarily. Use supported sub-user or access-management facilities where available.


### **Step 7: Log In and Review Your Dashboard**


Return to the login page and enter your newly created username and password.


Once logged in, review the functions available for your account, such as:


- IRN generation and management
- E-invoice reports
- Cancellation facilities
- User management
- API-related options
- Download and search utilities


The available menu items can vary by portal, account permissions, and the services enabled.


## **How to Log In to the E-Invoice Portal**


After completing registration, the **e invoice portal login** process is straightforward.


1. Open the IRP on which you registered.
2. Select the Login option.
3. Enter your authorised username and password.
4. Complete captcha or additional authentication, if requested.
5. Access the dashboard and choose the required function.


### **Can You Use Your Existing E-Way Bill Login?**


For the NIC-operated e-invoicing system, taxpayers with existing e-way bill portal credentials can generally use those credentials to access the corresponding e-invoice services.


This avoids unnecessary duplicate registration.


However, do not assume that the same username and password will work across all private IRPs. Some platforms follow separate account-creation and authentication processes.


### **What If You Forget Your Password?**


Use the password-recovery option on the relevant IRP.


Depending on the system, you may need to provide your username, GSTIN, captcha, or an OTP sent to your registered contact details.


If you're unable to recover access, contact the official helpdesk shown on that IRP rather than creating repeated accounts.


### **How Do You Choose the Right IRP?**


There is no single best portal for every business. Consider the following factors before selecting one.


**1. Existing access**


If your team already uses the NIC e-way bill system, the NIC IRP may be a convenient starting point.


**2. Software compatibility**


Check which IRP or API integration your billing or accounting software supports.


**3. Invoice volume**


A business issuing a few invoices may be comfortable with an available web or offline utility. A business processing hundreds of invoices may benefit from API-based automation.


**4. User access**


Check whether the chosen portal supports the access controls, user roles, and reports your accounting team needs.


**5. Support and operational continuity**


Consider official helpdesk availability and your internal backup process if your preferred reporting method becomes temporarily unavailable.


For most small businesses, the best option is the one that integrates reliably with their existing billing workflow without requiring repeated entry of invoice data.


## **What Happens After E-Invoice Registration?**


Registration only gives you access to the reporting system. It does not automatically generate an IRN for every invoice you create.


The e-invoicing process normally works as follows:


1. Create the invoice in your billing or accounting system.
2. Prepare the required invoice data according to the prescribed e-invoice schema.
3. Report the details through an authorised IRP using a supported method.
4. The IRP validates the submitted information.
5. If accepted, it returns an IRN and digitally signed QR code.
6. Incorporate the required IRN and QR code information into the invoice issued to the recipient.
7. Retain the invoice and acknowledgement details for reconciliation.


The reported information is also shared with GST systems for relevant downstream processes, including GSTR-1 auto-population.


For a detailed explanation of the full invoice-generation workflow, see GimBooks'[guide to creating e-invoices under GST](https://www.gimbooks.com/blog/how-to-create-e-invoices-under-gst/) .

## **Common E-Invoice Registration and Login Problems**


First-time users may experience problems when verifying their GSTIN, receiving an OTP, logging in, or configuring API access.


Here are common issues and practical ways to investigate them.


### **1. GSTIN Is Not Enabled for E-Invoicing**


**Possible cause:** Your GSTIN has not been enabled in the system, or the eligibility information requires review.


**What to do:** Check the official enablement status and compare it with your business's legal applicability. If required, complete the self-enablement process or use the official support channel.


### **2. OTP Is Not Received**


**Possible cause:** The contact information linked to GST registration may be outdated, or there may be a delivery issue.


**What to do:** Verify the registered contact details and retry according to the portal's instructions. If the information is incorrect, update it through the appropriate GST process.


### **3. Username or Password Is Incorrect**


**Possible cause:** You may be entering GST Common Portal credentials instead of your IRP credentials, or using credentials created for a different IRP.


**What to do:** Confirm the reporting portal, check your account details, and use the password-recovery facility where necessary.


### **4. Account Already Registered**


**Possible cause:** Your GSTIN or authorised user may already have an account on the relevant system.


**What to do:** Check with your accounting team or previous service provider before trying to register again. Recover existing credentials if appropriate.


### **5. Business Details Do Not Match**


**Possible cause:** There is a difference between the details stored on the IRP and the current GST registration records.


**What to do:** Verify the GST master data and use the supported refresh or correction process.


### **6. API Authentication Fails**


**Possible cause:** Incorrect API credentials, expired access, or incomplete API-user configuration.


**What to do:** Confirm the credentials and permissions required by your IRP and software provider. Do not use an ordinary website login password as an API credential unless the integration instructions explicitly require it.


### **7. IRN Generation Fails After Successful Login**


**Possible cause:** The submitted invoice may contain invalid data, duplicate document details, or other schema-validation errors.


**What to do:** Read the returned error message and correct the underlying invoice data or integration settings.


Remember that an IRN-generation error is not necessarily a login problem.


For more background on the e-invoice system and its terminology, read GimBooks'[e-invoicing overview](https://www.gimbooks.com/blog/everything-about-e-invoices/) .

### **How the Business Gets Started**

The accountant reviews the turnover history, transaction types, and exemptions to confirm that the business is covered.


**Step 2: Check GSTIN enablement**


The accountant checks whether the relevant GSTIN is enabled for e-invoicing.


**Step 3: Establish IRP access**


The business verifies whether existing e-way bill credentials can be used or whether new IRP onboarding is necessary.


**Step 4: Complete authentication**


The authorised user verifies the account using the registered contact information and completes the required setup.


**Step 5: Configure billing software**


The accountant connects the supported IRP integration to the billing software.

The team prepares a genuine eligible invoice, validates its details, submits it through the supported reporting process, and checks the returned IRN and QR code.

### **What Changes After Setup?**


Before integration, the accounts team might prepare invoices in one system and then separately upload their details for IRN generation.


With a compatible software integration, the team can work from the existing invoice record, reducing repeated data entry.


However, invoices still need to pass IRP validation, and the business remains responsible for accurate GST details.

## **Important E-Invoice Compliance Checks After Registration**


Successfully registering on an IRP is only the beginning. Businesses must continue reviewing their invoices and e-invoice records.


### **Check the Invoice Details Before Submission**


Verify supplier and buyer GSTINs, invoice number, document date, HSN/SAC, taxable value, GST amounts, and place of supply.


Incorrect details can cause invoice rejection or reporting errors.


### **Avoid Duplicate IRN Requests**


A document already registered with an IRN should not be repeatedly submitted as a new invoice.


Review the original acknowledgement and check the document status before attempting another submission.


### **Monitor Reporting Deadlines**


As of November 2026, taxpayers with aggregate annual turnover of ₹10 crore or more are subject to a 30-day reporting restriction for applicable invoices, credit notes, and debit notes, effective from 1 April 2025.


The restriction prevents reporting documents older than the permitted window to an IRP.


Other applicable taxpayers should still follow their legal e-invoicing obligations and avoid unnecessary reporting delays.


### **Understand Cancellation Rules**


Where an e-invoice needs to be cancelled, the applicable IRP cancellation facility generally permits cancellation within 24 hours of IRN generation, subject to system conditions.


A registered e-invoice cannot simply be edited on the IRP after generation. Corrections require the legally appropriate cancellation or amendment process.


### **Reconcile Your Records**


Maintain a record of:


- Original invoice number and date
- Customer GSTIN
- Invoice value and tax
- IRN
- IRN generation date
- E-invoice status
- Cancellation details, if any
- Relevant GST return reporting


A regular comparison between your sales register, IRN records, and GST return data helps identify discrepancies.


## **FAQs**


### **1. What is the official e-invoice portal in India?**


India has multiple authorised Invoice Registration Portals (IRPs). The first NIC-operated IRP is commonly used for e-invoice registration and reporting, while the GSTN master portal provides information, enablement checks, and verification facilities.


### **2. How do I register on the e-invoice portal?**


To register, confirm that your GSTIN is eligible and enabled, open an authorised IRP, select the taxpayer registration facility, enter the requested GSTIN details, complete OTP verification, and create the required login credentials.


Existing NIC e-way bill credentials may already provide access.


### **3. Is e-invoice registration free?**


Yes. Government-authorised IRPs provide the statutory IRN-generation service without a government generation fee. Optional third-party integrations, software subscriptions, or value-added services may have separate charges.


### **4. Can I use my GST portal login for e-invoicing?**


Not necessarily. The GST Common Portal and IRPs have different account systems. You may need separate IRP credentials, although existing NIC e-way bill credentials can generally be used with the corresponding NIC e-invoice system.


### **5. How can I check my GSTIN's e-invoice status?**


Use the taxpayer enablement facility available through the official GST e-invoice information system. Enter the GSTIN and review its status. Remember that enablement and legal applicability are not identical.


### **6. How many e-invoice IRPs are available in India?**


The GSTN guidance identifies six authorised Invoice Registration Portals, operated through NIC and approved private service providers.


### **7. Do I need to register on all six IRPs?**


No. A business can choose an authorised IRP that supports its reporting method. Additional onboarding may be required if the business uses another provider, but registration on every IRP is not a general requirement.


### **8. Can I generate an e-invoice without logging into an IRP website every time?**


Yes. Compatible billing or accounting software can report invoice information through an authorised API integration. Initial registration, authentication, or API configuration may still be required.


### **9. What happens if my e-invoice portal account is already registered?**


Check whether your organisation previously created an account or already uses compatible e-way bill credentials. Use the relevant recovery facility instead of creating unnecessary duplicate accounts.


### **10. Can I change my e-invoice after generating an IRN?**


The registered invoice details cannot be directly edited on the IRP after IRN generation. Where permitted, the IRN may be cancelled within the applicable cancellation window. Other corrections must follow the relevant GST procedures.


### **11. What is the difference between an IRP and an IRN?**


An **Invoice Registration Portal (IRP)** is the authorised system used for registering invoice details. An **Invoice Reference Number (IRN)** is the unique reference generated when an eligible document is successfully registered.


### **12. Can GimBooks generate e-invoices without manual JSON uploads?**


GimBooks supports integrated e-invoice generation using the configured IRP API connection. After setup, users can initiate e-invoice generation from eligible invoices in their billing workflow, subject to successful authentication and IRP validation.


## **Conclusion**


Getting started with the **einvoice portal** becomes easier when you understand the difference between GST registration, e-invoice enablement, IRP account creation, and actual IRN generation.


For a first-time user, the most important steps are confirming applicability, checking GSTIN enablement, choosing an authorised IRP, completing account verification, and selecting a reporting method that fits the business.


Once the initial setup is complete, integrated billing software such as GimBooks can help reduce repetitive invoice entry and make regular e-invoice reporting more manageable.
